messages:
inc-bot: [ALERT] node=gpu-03 service=runtime severity=critical metric=cuda_oom count=3 headroom_reported=1.18GiB first_seen=2026-03-15T09:12:06Z

alice_g: seeing repeated OOMs on gpu-03. headroom reported by telemetry but containers still crash with CUDA OOM. root container id: 8fa3b2. Logs show repeated allocation failures during kv-cache prefetch.

alice_g: paste logs: 
```
[2026-03-15T09:11:58Z] allocator: request 1.2GiB for kv-prefetch failed - CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY (2)
[2026-03-15T09:11:59Z] reserve: reserved_blocks=4 reserved_size=3.0GiB headroom=1.18GiB free_total=900MiB fragmented=1.1GiB
[2026-03-15T09:12:00Z] runtime: container 8fa3b2 died with signal SIGABRT
```

ben_sre: oncall here. not seeing node-level GPU memory exhaustion across all processes; looks like fragmentation + shadow reservations. can you confirm nv-smi snapshot?

alice_g: nv-smi output attached inline: 
```
GPU 0: 24GiB total, used=20.3GiB, processes: runtime(4) runtime(3) prefetch(2)
Memory free ~3.7GiB but many small free chunks.
```

carla_ml: this smells like reserve drift plus stale kv-cache pages. we recently tweaked dynamic-reserve logic (AUTO_RESERVE_RATIO bump last night). If dynamic reserve splits across multiple slabs, fragmentation increases.

devin_runtime: quick mitigation options: 1) disable kv-prefetch on node 2) force evict KV cache and reclaim 3) reduce concurrent request slots for gpu-03 4) flip dynamic-reserve=false (hot config)

ben_sre: priority to restore customer-facing endpoints. who can run an immediate cache-evict?

alice_g: I can. evicting KV cache for node gpu-03 now.

alice_g: running command: 
```bash
# admin API - evict per-node kv cache
curl -XPOST -H 'Authorization: Bearer $S' https://admin.internal/nodes/gpu-03/actions -d '{"action":"evict_kv_cache"}'
```

alice_g: eviction initiated, monitoring. also lowering concurrency limit on that node: set-concurrency gpu-03 4 -> 2 (temporary).

inc-bot: [NOTE] action=evict_kv_cache status=started node=gpu-03 actor=alice_g

carla_ml: also please disable prefetch for models using large KV shards (prefix=llama-heavy) on that node. I'll post a small runtime config patch.

devin_runtime: pushing safe-spill toggle to true on gpu-03 (forces spill-to-CPU fallback earlier to avoid OOM) - patch id: r/12345. Applying as a canary on gpu-03 only.

devin_runtime: command applied: 
```bash
kubectl patch deployment runtime-gpu-03 -p '{"spec":{"template":{"metadata":{"annotations":{"runtime/safe-spill":"true"}}}}}'
```

alice_g: after evict and safe-spill flip we saw 5-10% reduction in 500s on /v1/generate; latency improved slightly. still seeing one more crash at 09:22.

ben_sre: we need a longer-term mitigation while we triage allocator behavior. options: bump sparepool to reserve ephemeral blocks, or increase reserved_blocks size to reduce fragmentation overhead. Which is less risky?

carla_ml: bump sparepool by 512MiB is low-risk and reversible. increasing reserved block size might worsen fragmentation if not aligned with slab sizes. I'd vote sparepool bump + collect heaps.

devin_runtime: rolling a hotfix: sparepool +512MiB + telemetry toggles to surface slab fragmentation metrics. PR r/12367. Applying to gpu-03 then to the pool.

on-technical update (alice_g): customer impact: about 0.8% of requests to hosted chat were 500s for ~10 minutes during the peak. Top affected customers: 2 sandbox apps, 1 mid-market account reported degraded latency. No data loss reported.

oncall-bot: handing off to ben_sre for continued monitoring and postmortem; current status: partial mitigation in place, node under watch. summary: suspected allocator/reserve telemetry mismatch leading to visible headroom but unusable fragmented memory; mitigation = kv-evict + safe-spill + sparepool bump.

ben_sre: picking up. next steps: 1) keep node drained for non-critical rollouts; 2) collect heapdumps and per-slab fragmentation metrics (devin, carla) 3) evaluate reverting AUTO_RESERVE_RATIO tweak from last night 4) schedule a 30-min postmortem after incident closure.

carla_ml: how to collect heapdump: devin, can you run allocator snapshot on gpu-03? command below: 
```bash
# allocate debug snapshot
ssh admin@gpu-03 'sudo /opt/runtime/bin/allocator_dump --output /tmp/alloc-snap-$(date +%s).json'
scp admin@gpu-03:/tmp/alloc-snap-*.json ./
```

devin_runtime: snapshot taken at 2026-03-15T09:35:12Z and uploaded to /mnt/telemetry/incidents/3524009876/alloc-snap-09-35.json. Saved trace id trace-3524009876.

ben_sre: will start a controlled roll of similar nodes with sparepool bump tomorrow if traces confirm fragmentation root cause. For now we mark incident as mitigated but not resolved.

alice_g: follow-up action items created: INC-352400 (collect more snapshots, run allocator sim on staging with AUTO_RESERVE_RATIO revert, add alert for fragmentation ratio >0.45).

inc-bot: [UPDATE] incident_state=mitigated mitigations=evict_kv_cache,safe_spill,sparepool_bump

ben_sre: final note — customer impact slice: 0.8% errors for 10m window, no SLA hits yet but trending. scheduling postmortem and responsible owners: devin_runtime (fix), carla_ml (root cause analysis), alice_g (pager/ops), ben_sre (postmortem writeup).

on-incident follow-up (carla_ml): propose we add a periodic fragmentation scoring job that computes: fragmentation = 1 - (largest_contiguous_free / total_free) and alert if > 0.5. also add per-node reserved_block alignment telemetry.

on-incident follow-up (devin_runtime): will open PR r/12410 to revert AUTO_RESERVE_RATIO and add more conservative defaults for dynamic-reserve on nodes with small-slab GPUs.

ben_sre: closing the Slack thread for live ops; keep monitoring dashboards for 2 hours then promote to postmortem. thanks all. :thumbsup:
